Arch Ophthalmol 1997; 115: 865–72. Angiomatous disease. Encouraging responses were reported in 4 of 5 children treated with interferon alfa-2a for various angi- omatous diseases.1 Regression of haemangioma size by more than 50% was achieved in 11 of 18 infants and children given interferon alfa-2a for 1 to 5 months,2 and in 11 of 19 children treated for at least 4 months.3 Interferon alfa-2b has also been found to cause regression of haemangioma in 27 of 38 children treated for at least 6 months.4 In addition, there have been reports of the successful use of interferon alfa-2b to treat infantile giant cell angioblastoma5 and pelvic metastases of adult haemangioen- dothelioma of the liver.6 The use of interferons as anti-angiogenic agents has been re- viewed.7 1.
